items.prompt: After his visit to the temple at age twelve, the boy Jesus returned with Mary and Joseph to the town marked on the map and was subject unto them. Which town is it?
items.explanation: Luke 2:51 says Jesus went down with his parents and came to Nazareth, where he was subject unto them.
items.hint: This Galilean hometown later gave Jesus a title: 'of ...'.

items.prompt: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judaea, where wise men from the east came seeking him. Which marker shows Bethlehem?
items.explanation: Matthew 2:1 records that Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod, and wise men came from the east.
items.hint: Look in the hill country of Judea, just south of Jerusalem.

items.prompt: Leaving Nazareth, Jesus came and dwelt in the town marked on the map, upon the sea coast in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim. Which town is it?
items.explanation: Matthew 4:13 says that, leaving Nazareth, Jesus came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast.
items.hint: This town sits on the northern shore of a freshwater lake.

items.prompt: Jesus raised the only son of a widow as his funeral procession left the gate of a city called Nain. Which marker shows Nain?
items.explanation: Luke 7:11-15 tells how Jesus went into a city called Nain and raised the dead son of a widow, delivering him to his mother.
items.hint: This village lies in lower Galilee, not far from Nazareth and Mount Tabor.

items.prompt: Jesus entered and passed through the city marked on the map, where a chief publican named Zacchaeus climbed a sycomore tree to see him. Which city is it?
items.explanation: Luke 19:1-5 records that Jesus passed through Jericho, where Zacchaeus climbed a sycomore tree and Jesus called him down.
items.hint: This ancient city lies in the Jordan valley, near the north end of the Dead Sea.

items.prompt: Lazarus, whom Jesus raised from the dead, lived in Bethany, the town of Mary and her sister Martha. Which marker shows Bethany?
items.explanation: John 11:1 introduces Lazarus of Bethany, the town of Mary and her sister Martha.
items.hint: This village lies just east of Jerusalem, beyond the Mount of Olives.

items.prompt: Walking beside the body of water marked on the map, Jesus saw Simon Peter and Andrew casting a net, for they were fishers. Which body of water is it?
items.explanation: Matthew 4:18 says Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw Simon called Peter and Andrew casting a net into the sea.
items.hint: This freshwater lake lies in the north, fed by the Jordan.

items.prompt: Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John. Which marker shows the Jordan?
items.explanation: Matthew 3:13 records that Jesus came from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.
items.hint: Look for the river running north to south through the rift valley, far from the coast.

items.prompt: On the night he was betrayed, Jesus went with his disciples to the place marked on the map and told them to sit while he went to pray. Which place is it?
items.explanation: Matthew 26:36 says Jesus came with his disciples unto a place called Gethsemane and told them to sit while he went to pray.
items.hint: This garden lay just outside Jerusalem's eastern wall.

items.prompt: Jesus departed into the coasts of Tyre and Sidon, where a woman of Canaan begged him to heal her daughter. Which marker shows Tyre?
items.explanation: Matthew 15:21-22 says Jesus departed into the coasts of Tyre and Sidon, and a woman of Canaan cried to him for her daughter.
items.hint: This Phoenician port lies on the Mediterranean coast, north of Galilee.

batch.topic: the life and ministry of Jesus in Galilee, Samaria and Judea

items.prompt: After capturing the ark of God, the Philistines brought it into the house of their god Dagon in the city marked on the map. Which city is it?
items.explanation: The Philistines took the ark of God from Ebenezer to Ashdod and set it in the house of Dagon (1 Samuel 5:1-2).
items.hint: It was one of the five Philistine lords' cities on the coastal plain.

items.prompt: Samson rose at midnight and carried off the doors of the city gate of Gaza. Which marker shows Gaza?
items.explanation: Samson went to Gaza, then rose at midnight and took the doors of the city gate up to a hill before Hebron (Judges 16:1-3).
items.hint: Look for the southernmost Philistine city on the coast.

items.prompt: Samson went down to Ashkelon and slew thirty men to pay the wager over his riddle. Which marker shows Ashkelon?
items.explanation: The Spirit of the LORD came upon Samson, and he went down to Ashkelon and slew thirty men, giving their garments to those who expounded the riddle (Judges 14:19).
items.hint: This Philistine city lay on the Mediterranean shore.

items.prompt: When the ark of God was sent to the city marked on the map, its people cried out that it had been brought to slay them. Which city is it?
items.explanation: The Philistines sent the ark of God to Ekron, and the Ekronites cried out in fear (1 Samuel 5:10).
items.hint: It was the Philistine city closest to the hill country of Judah, the last stop before the ark was sent back.

items.prompt: The king of the city marked on the map sent his servants to Solomon and supplied cedar for the temple. Which city is it?
items.explanation: Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants unto Solomon, for he had always loved David (1 Kings 5:1).
items.hint: A famous Phoenician seaport north of Israel.

items.prompt: God sent Elijah to Zarephath, where a widow fed him during the drought. Which marker shows Zarephath?
items.explanation: The LORD told Elijah to go to Zarephath, which belonged to Zidon, where a widow woman would sustain him (1 Kings 17:9-10).
items.hint: The text says this town belonged to Zidon, on the Phoenician coast.

items.prompt: Fleeing from the presence of the LORD, Jonah went down to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish. Which marker shows Joppa?
items.explanation: Jonah went down to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish (Jonah 1:3).
items.hint: He needed a seaport on the Mediterranean.

items.prompt: Fleeing the Philistines, the men of Israel fell down slain on the mountain marked on the map, where Saul and his sons died. Which mountain is it?
items.explanation: The men of Israel fled from the Philistines and fell down slain in mount Gilboa, and the Philistines slew Saul's sons (1 Samuel 31:1-2).
items.hint: It rises above the Jezreel valley's eastern end.

items.prompt: In the battle to defend Gibeon, Joshua said, 'Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon.' Which marker shows Gibeon?
items.explanation: Joshua spoke to the LORD and said, 'Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon' (Joshua 10:12).
items.hint: This town lay in the hill country of Benjamin, just north of Jerusalem.

items.prompt: Hezekiah sent a message of submission to the king of Assyria while he was encamped at the city marked on the map. Which city is it?
items.explanation: After Sennacherib took the fenced cities of Judah, Hezekiah sent to the king of Assyria to Lachish, saying, 'I have offended' (2 Kings 18:13-14).
items.hint: A major fortified city in the lowlands of Judah, southwest of Jerusalem.

batch.topic: cities of the Philistines, Phoenicia and the coast, and battles of Israel

items.prompt: Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven and named the place where he slept. Which town is marked on the map?
items.explanation: After dreaming of a ladder set up on the earth that reached to heaven, Jacob called the name of that place Bethel, formerly Luz (Genesis 28:12-19).
items.hint: The name means 'house of God'.

items.prompt: After Israel crossed the Jordan, the LORD told Joshua that this city's wall would fall down flat when the people shouted. Which city is marked on the map?
items.explanation: The LORD said, 'I have given into thine hand Jericho,' and promised that after the trumpets and the shout the wall of the city would fall down flat (Joshua 6:2-5).
items.hint: Israel marched around this city once a day for six days.

items.prompt: Samson carried off the doors of the city gate of Gaza. Which marker shows Gaza?
items.explanation: Samson went to Gaza, and at midnight he took the doors of the gate of the city and carried them away (Judges 16:1-3).
items.hint: Look for a Philistine city near the southern coast.

items.prompt: Terah left Ur with Abram, Sarai and Lot, heading for Canaan, but they stopped and dwelt in the city marked on the map. Which city is it?
items.explanation: Terah and his family went forth from Ur of the Chaldees to go into Canaan, but they came unto Haran and dwelt there (Genesis 11:31).
items.hint: This city lies in the north, along the route from Mesopotamia toward Canaan.

items.prompt: The LORD reminded Abram that He had brought him out of Ur of the Chaldees. Which marker shows Ur?
items.explanation: The LORD said to Abram, 'I am the LORD that brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give thee this land' (Genesis 15:7).
items.hint: Look in southern Mesopotamia, near the lower Euphrates.

items.prompt: Abraham buried Sarah in the cave of Machpelah, near the city of Hebron. Which marker shows Hebron?
items.explanation: Abraham buried Sarah in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre, 'the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan' (Genesis 23:19).
items.hint: It lies in the hill country of Judah, south of Jerusalem.

items.prompt: Abraham and Abimelech made a covenant at a well, and Abraham named the place after the oath they swore. Which place is marked on the map?
items.explanation: Abraham called that place Beersheba 'because there they sware both of them' (Genesis 21:31).
items.hint: Its name is linked to a well and an oath, in the Negev.

items.prompt: Returning from Padanaram, Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, and pitched his tent before it. Which marker shows Shechem?
items.explanation: Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padanaram, and pitched his tent before the city (Genesis 33:18).
items.hint: Look in the central hill country, north of Bethel.

items.prompt: Deborah told Barak to gather ten thousand men and draw toward the mountain marked on the map. Which mountain is it?
items.explanation: Deborah called Barak and told him, 'Go and draw toward mount Tabor, and take with thee ten thousand men' (Judges 4:6).
items.hint: This rounded mountain rises from the plain in lower Galilee.

items.prompt: Moses recalled that the spies were sent from Kadesh-barnea to see the land. Which marker shows Kadesh-barnea?
items.explanation: Moses reminded the tribes that their fathers did the same 'when I sent them from Kadeshbarnea to see the land' (Numbers 32:8).
items.hint: Look in the wilderness far to the south, beyond the Negev.

batch.topic: the patriarchs, the exodus and the judges

items.prompt: Saul was approaching the city marked on the map when a light from heaven shone around him. Which city is it?
items.explanation: Acts 9:3 says that as Saul journeyed, he came near Damascus, and suddenly a light from heaven shone round about him.
items.hint: Saul was traveling there with letters to arrest believers, and it was an ancient city of Syria.

items.prompt: After his voyage and shipwreck, Paul arrived as a prisoner in Rome, where he was allowed to dwell by himself with a soldier guarding him. Which marker shows Rome?
items.explanation: Acts 28:16 records that when they came to Rome, Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.
items.hint: Look for the imperial capital on the Italian peninsula.

items.prompt: Paul stood in the midst of Mars' hill and addressed the men of the city marked on the map about an altar to the unknown god. Which city is it?
items.explanation: In Acts 17:22-23 Paul stood on Mars' hill and said, 'Ye men of Athens,' referring to their altar inscribed TO THE UNKNOWN GOD.
items.hint: This Greek city was famous for its philosophers.

items.prompt: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul passed through the upper coasts and came to Ephesus, where he found certain disciples. Which marker shows Ephesus?
items.explanation: Acts 19:1 says that while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul came to Ephesus and found certain disciples there.
items.hint: It was a major port on the western coast of Asia Minor.

items.prompt: Paul came to the city marked on the map, the chief city of that part of Macedonia, where Lydia, a seller of purple, heard him by the riverside. Which city is it?
items.explanation: Acts 16:12-14 describes Philippi as the chief city of that part of Macedonia and a colony, where Lydia heard Paul by a river side.
items.hint: It was a Roman colony and the first stop inland after Paul crossed from Asia into Macedonia.

items.prompt: John was on the isle called Patmos for the word of God and the testimony of Jesus Christ when he received his revelation. Which marker shows Patmos?
items.explanation: Revelation 1:9 says John was in the isle that is called Patmos, for the word of God and the testimony of Jesus Christ.
items.hint: Look for a small island in the Aegean Sea, off the coast of Asia Minor.

items.prompt: After leaving Athens, Paul came to the city marked on the map and stayed with Aquila and Priscilla, because they shared the same craft as tentmakers. Which city is it?
items.explanation: Acts 18:1-3 says Paul departed from Athens and came to Corinth, where he lived and worked with Aquila and Priscilla, for they were tentmakers.
items.hint: This Greek city lay on the narrow isthmus west of Athens.

items.prompt: Passing by Mysia, Paul came down to Troas, where he saw a vision of a man of Macedonia saying, 'Come over into Macedonia, and help us.' Which marker shows Troas?
items.explanation: Acts 16:8-9 records that Paul came down to Troas, and a vision appeared to him in the night of a man of Macedonia asking for help.
items.hint: Look for a port in the far northwest of Asia Minor, facing across the sea toward Macedonia.

items.prompt: In the town marked on the map, Paul healed a man who had been a cripple from his mother's womb and had never walked. Which town is it?
items.explanation: Acts 14:8-10 says there sat a certain man at Lystra, a cripple from his mother's womb, who leaped and walked when Paul told him to stand upright.
items.hint: After this miracle, the crowd mistook Paul and Barnabas for gods.

items.prompt: The brethren sent Paul and Silas by night unto Berea, where the people were more noble than those in Thessalonica and searched the scriptures daily. Which marker shows Berea?
items.explanation: Acts 17:10-11 says Paul and Silas were sent unto Berea, whose people received the word with readiness and searched the scriptures daily.
items.hint: It lay in Macedonia, west of Thessalonica, in northern Greece.

batch.topic: the early church and Paul's journeys

items.prompt: Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal on the mountain marked on the map. Which mountain is it?
items.explanation: Elijah told Ahab to gather all Israel and the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal unto mount Carmel (1 Kings 18:19-20).
items.hint: This ridge runs down to the Mediterranean coast near modern Haifa.

items.prompt: Jesus saw Simon and Andrew casting a net as he walked by the Sea of Galilee. Which marker shows the Sea of Galilee?
items.explanation: Mark 1:16 says Jesus walked by the sea of Galilee and saw Simon and Andrew casting a net into the sea.
items.hint: Look for the freshwater lake in the north, fed by the Jordan.

items.prompt: Jesus came from Galilee to be baptized by John in the river marked on the map. Which river is it?
items.explanation: Matthew 3:13 records that Jesus came from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.
items.hint: This river flows north to south, linking two seas.

items.prompt: King Saul and his sons fell in battle against the Philistines on Mount Gilboa. Which marker shows Mount Gilboa?
items.explanation: The men of Israel fell down slain in mount Gilboa, and Saul took a sword and fell upon it (1 Samuel 31:1-4).
items.hint: It overlooks the eastern end of the Jezreel Valley.

items.prompt: Jacob sent his family across the ford of the river marked on the map, then wrestled with a man until daybreak. Which river is it?
items.explanation: Jacob passed over the ford Jabbok, and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day (Genesis 32:22-24).
items.hint: An eastern tributary that joins the Jordan from the hills of Gilead.

items.prompt: Genesis names the Euphrates as the fourth of the rivers flowing out of Eden. Which marker shows the Euphrates?
items.explanation: Genesis 2:10-14 describes a river going out of Eden that parted into four heads, and the fourth river is Euphrates.
items.hint: This great river runs through Mesopotamia toward the Persian Gulf.

items.prompt: On the night of his betrayal, Jesus went with his disciples, as he was wont, to the hill marked on the map. Which hill is it?
items.explanation: Luke 22:39 says Jesus came out and went, as he was wont, to the mount of Olives, and his disciples followed him.
items.hint: It rises just east of Jerusalem across a valley.

items.prompt: After the flood, Noah's ark came to rest upon the mountains of Ararat. Which marker shows Ararat?
items.explanation: Genesis 8:4 states that the ark rested in the seventh month upon the mountains of Ararat.
items.hint: Look to the highlands far north of Mesopotamia.

items.prompt: In Abram's day, kings joined battle in the vale of Siddim, 'which is the salt sea.' Which marker shows the Salt Sea?
items.explanation: Genesis 14:3 says the kings were joined together in the vale of Siddim, which is the salt sea.
items.hint: It lies at the southern end of the Jordan River.

items.prompt: Fleeing from Absalom, King David passed over the brook marked on the map as he left Jerusalem. Which brook is it?
items.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:23 records that the king himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over toward the wilderness.
items.hint: This brook runs in the valley between Jerusalem and the Mount of Olives.

batch.topic: mountains, rivers, seas and valleys of the Bible

items.prompt: After the great fish, the LORD sent Jonah a second time to preach to Nineveh, 'an exceeding great city.' Which marker shows Nineveh?
items.explanation: Jonah 3:3 says Jonah 'went unto Nineveh, according to the word of the LORD,' a city of three days' journey. Nineveh lay on the Tigris in Assyria.
items.hint: Look along the Tigris in the heart of Assyria, north of Babylonia.

items.prompt: Nebuchadnezzar carried King Jehoiachin, his household and the mighty of the land away captive to the city marked on the map. Which city is it?
items.explanation: 2 Kings 24:15 records that Nebuchadnezzar 'carried away Jehoiachin to Babylon,' taking them 'into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon.'
items.hint: It was the capital of Nebuchadnezzar's own empire, on the Euphrates.

items.prompt: Elijah challenged Ahab to gather all Israel and the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal to Mount Carmel. Which marker shows Mount Carmel?
items.explanation: In 1 Kings 18:19 Elijah tells Ahab to 'gather to me all Israel unto mount Carmel' with the prophets of Baal. Carmel is the ridge reaching the Mediterranean coast in the north.
items.hint: This mountain ridge juts out toward the sea on Israel's northern coast.

items.prompt: Nehemiah was in 'Shushan the palace,' serving the Persian king, when he heard of Jerusalem's broken walls. Which city is marked on the map?
items.explanation: Nehemiah 1:1 says Nehemiah was 'in Shushan the palace' in the month Chisleu. Shushan (Susa) was a royal city of the Persian kings, east of the Tigris.
items.hint: This Persian royal city lies east of Mesopotamia, toward the Zagros mountains.

items.prompt: King Omri bought a hill from Shemer for two talents of silver and built a city on it, naming it Samaria. Which marker shows Samaria?
items.explanation: 1 Kings 16:24 tells how Omri 'bought the hill Samaria of Shemer for two talents of silver' and named the city after him. It became the capital of the northern kingdom.
items.hint: It was the northern kingdom's capital, in the hill country north of Jerusalem.

items.prompt: After Jerusalem fell, King Zedekiah was captured and brought up to the king of Babylon, who passed judgment on him at the town marked on the map. Which town is it?
items.explanation: 2 Kings 25:6 says 'they took the king, and brought him up to the king of Babylon to Riblah; and they gave judgment upon him.' Riblah lay in Syria on the Orontes.
items.hint: Nebuchadnezzar held his field headquarters here in Syria, far north of Jerusalem.

items.prompt: The prophet Amos was 'among the herdmen' of the town marked on the map. Which town is it?
items.explanation: Amos 1:1 introduces 'The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa.' Tekoa was a village in Judah south of Bethlehem.
items.hint: Amos came from a small Judean village on the edge of the wilderness, south of Bethlehem.

items.prompt: During the drought the LORD told Elijah to go to Zarephath, where a widow woman would sustain him. Which marker shows Zarephath?
items.explanation: 1 Kings 17:9 commands, 'get thee to Zarephath, which belongeth to Zidon,' where a widow woman would feed him. It lay on the Phoenician coast between Tyre and Sidon.
items.hint: The verse says it belonged to Zidon, so look on the northern coast.

items.prompt: Against Jeremiah's warning, the remnant of Judah fled into Egypt and came to Tahpanhes, taking the prophet with them. Which marker shows Tahpanhes?
items.explanation: Jeremiah 43:7 says 'they came into the land of Egypt... thus came they even to Tahpanhes.' It was a border city in the eastern Nile Delta.
items.hint: The refugees went into Egypt, so look in the eastern Nile Delta.

items.prompt: Naboth's vineyard, coveted by King Ahab, lay in the town marked on the map, close by Ahab's palace. Which town is it?
items.explanation: 1 Kings 21:1 says Naboth 'had a vineyard, which was in Jezreel, hard by the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.'
items.hint: Naboth's hometown gave its name to the broad northern valley below Mount Gilboa.

batch.topic: the kings, prophets, exile and the empires around Israel
